In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

We open this meeting of ours, which is the second meeting of the month of Rabi' al-Thani, on Thursday the twenty-first of Rabi' al-Thani in the year one thousand four hundred and fourteen, and we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to bless us all in our lifespans and our deeds, to make the best of our lives their last part, the best of our deeds their conclusions, and the best and happiest of our days the day we meet Him.

These blessed gatherings between people, between scholars and students of knowledge, and between students of knowledge and the common folk, are without doubt beneficial and good gatherings, which make people gain insight into their religion, grow close to one another, and share with one another their needs and their calamities. There is no wonder in that, for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it strengthening the other" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2446) and Muslim (2585/65), from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]], and he, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, their mercy and their compassion is like the likeness of a single body: when one of its limbs complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6011) and Muslim (2586/66), with his wording, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, their mercy and their compassion is the likeness of the body; when a limb of it complains, the rest of the body responds to it with sleeplessness and fever."]]. This is what is obligatory upon the Islamic nation: that it be one body, so that when one limb of it is in pain, the rest of the body feels its pain until it recovers and is at rest; and likewise they must be like a building, one part strengthening the other. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, interlaced his fingers to indicate that the more a building is tightly joined and fitted together, the stronger it is.

Our meetings, praise be to Allah, contain blessing; those present benefit from them, those listening benefit from them, and those who hear benefit from them, through what Allah has bestowed upon us in this age of the widespread availability of audio cassettes among people. A person can be driving his car while listening to the Shaykh speaking to him without fatigue and without boredom, and a person can be lying in his bed listening to knowledge. All of this is by the grace Allah has bestowed upon us through these cassettes. For this reason we see, praise be to Allah, the effects of these cassettes in homes, among the young and the old, the women and the men, and this is without doubt good and blessing.

It is our custom to open the meeting with discussion of verses of the Noble Qur'an, which we began with Surat al-Naba' until we reached Surat al-Buruj. We chose this portion because it is frequently heard from people in the prayers. The Noble Qur'an was not sent down merely for recitation; rather it was sent down for recitation, for reflection (tadabbur), and for remembrance (tadhakkur), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾ [Sad 29]. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, would not go beyond ten verses until they had learned them and what they contained of knowledge and action [[Al-Tahawi narrated in Mushkil al-Athar (1452), from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: Our companions used to teach us and inform us that the Prophet ﷺ would teach one of them ten verses, and he would not move on from them until he had learned the action in them. He said: And they said: "We learned the Qur'an and the action together."]].

Whoever has no share of the Qur'an except recitation is, in reality, unlettered (ummi), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book except wishful thinking﴾ [al-Baqarah 78]; i.e., except recitation. So He described them as unlettered even though they recite. Therefore Muslims must learn the meanings of the Qur'an. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book called Muqaddimah fi 'Ilm al-Tafsir: If people were given a book to study in medicine or in any other science, they must understand its meaning in order to benefit from it. If this is the case with scientific books that are the words of humans, how much more so with the mother of knowledge and the root of knowledge, which is the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic! It is more fitting and more deserving that we attend to it, know its meaning and its interpretation, and receive it from the imams of tafsir (tafsir: explanation of the Qur'an) who are known for soundness of creed and correctness of method.

We have reached Surat al-Buruj. Allah, glorified and exalted, says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿By the sky containing great stars (1) and the promised Day (2)﴾ [al-Buruj 1, 2].

The basmalah (basmalah: the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful") is an independent verse in the Noble Book, not part of the surah before it nor of the surah after it. It is recited at the beginning of every surah except Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), because the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did not write it at the start of that surah, so it remained without a basmalah. What is widespread among the common folk, that the jinn snatched the basmalah of Surat Bara'ah, is without doubt false, because Allah says: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr 9]; and it is not possible for the devils or the jinn to be given power over it so as to snatch from it. Rather, Allah protected it at the time of its revelation and protected it after its revelation. What is mentioned from some scholars, that the basmalah was not mentioned in it because it was revealed with the sword, since it contains the command to fight the polytheists, is also not correct, because the basmalah is a blessing, and jihad in the way of Allah is among the greatest things in which blessing is sought. In any case, it is an independent verse at the beginning of every surah except Surat Bara'ah.

It is not part of al-Fatihah according to the preponderant opinion, which is indicated by the sacred hadith, in which Allah, blessed and exalted, says, as His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, related from Him: "I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, He says: My servant has praised Me..." until the end of the hadith. This indicates that the basmalah is not part of al-Fatihah. Likewise, the first thing revealed to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, was Surat Iqra' (al-'Alaq), which Jibril recited to him, and the basmalah was not in it. This indicates that it is not part of the surah.

Allah's statement: ﴿By the sky containing great stars﴾ [al-Buruj 1]. The waw here is a particle of oath; meaning Allah swears by the sky containing great stars, i.e., possessing them.

Al-buruj is the plural of burj, which is a great group of stars. They were called burUj (towers) because of their height, elevation, prominence and clarity. According to astronomers, the burj (zodiac constellations) are twelve, gathered in the verse of the poet:

Hamal, then Thawr, then Jawza', then Saratan,
Then Asad, Sunbula, then Mizan,
Then 'Aqrab, Qaws, then Jady, and likewise
Dalw, and the last of them is Hitan.

So they are twelve towers: three of them for spring, three for summer, three for autumn, and three for winter. Allah swears by the sky containing the towers, and He may swear by whatever He wills of His creation. As for us, we do not swear except by Allah, by His names and attributes, and we do not swear by any created thing, because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "Whoever is going to swear, let him swear by Allah or remain silent" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2679) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]], and his saying: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed kufr" or: "has committed shirk" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1535) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]].

﴿By the sky containing great stars﴾: so ﴿containing great stars﴾ means possessing them, namely the great group of stars, and in the sky there are twelve towers.

﴿And by the promised day﴾ [Al-Buruj: 2]. The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah, glory be to Him, promised and explained in His Book, and for which He set up rational proofs showing that it will certainly come to pass, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As We initiated the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing [it]﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 104].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 85, verse 3:

﴿By the witness and the witnessed.﴾ [Al-Buruj: 3] The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) have mentioned several opinions regarding "the witness" and "the witnessed," which all come together in this: Allah swore an oath by every witness and by everything witnessed. Witnesses are many. Among them is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is a witness over us. Among them are we, this Ummah, who are witnesses over mankind. Among them are the parts of the human body, which on the Day of Resurrection will testify against a person for what he did of good and evil. Among them are the angels, who will bear witness on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever bears witness to the truth is included in His saying: ﴿and a witness﴾.

As for "the witnessed," it is the Day of Resurrection and what will be displayed on it of great terrors, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day that will be witnessed.﴾ [Hud: 103] So Allah swore by every witness and by everything witnessed.

﴿The promised Day﴾ (Al-Yawm al-Mawud): what is it?

* Students: The Day of Resurrection.

* The Shaykh: The Day of Resurrection.

"Destroyed were the companions of the trench" (Qur'an 85:4). "Destroyed" means: ruined, cursed. It was also said that "qutila" here means "cursed," that is, expelled and removed from the mercy of God.

"The companions of the trench" (ashab al-ukhdud) are a people of disbelievers who burned the believers in fire. Several accounts have been related about these people, one of them in al-Sham and another in Yemen. The point is that these disbelievers tried to make the believers renounce their religion, but they failed. So they dug a trench (ukhdud), long pits in the earth like a river, gathered a great quantity of firewood, and burned the believers in it, may God protect us. This is why He said: "The fire fueled with wood" (Qur'an 85:5). That is, the trench was a trench of fire. "Fueled with wood" means: abundant blazing firewood.

"Destroyed were the companions of the trench" (Qur'an 85:4). "Destroyed" means: ruined, cursed. It was also said that "qutila" here means "cursed," that is, expelled and removed from the mercy of God.

The point is that these disbelievers tried to make the believers renounce their religion, but they failed. ﷻ﴿إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌ﴾ [al-Buruj: 6] Meaning: those who dug the trenches and threw the believers into them were, may Allah protect us, people of harshness and tyranny. They watched the fire consuming these human beings while they sat beside it on their thrones, enjoying themselves as though nothing had happened, may Allah protect us. This is from tyranny: that a person sees human beings being consumed by fire while he sits on his throne, entertaining himself with conversation, and does not care.

And they are witnesses to what they did to the believers. (Q. 85:7)

That is, they are witnesses to what they did to the believers; i.e., they were present, and what they did to the believers was not hidden from them. That is why they deserved this threat, indeed they deserved this punishment: that Allah destroyed them, cursed them, expelled them, and removed them far from His mercy.

We ask Allah, glorified and exalted be He, to end our lives and yours with goodness, and to grant us and all Muslims a good end.

We had discussed the opening verses of Surah al-Buruj last week, until we reached Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Al-Buruj 8]. That is, those who set fire to the ditch and burned these believers did not object to anything except this: that they believed in Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.﴾ This objection deserves to be objected to, because a believer in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, should be supported, assisted, and have his path made easy. As for being prevented and deterred, to the point of being burned in fire, there is no doubt that this is a great transgression. Yet these people are not to be blamed for it; rather, they deserve praise, because they worshipped the One who deserves worship, Allah, the Exalted, who created creation so that they would worship Him. Whoever performs this worship has recognized the wisdom behind creation and given it its due.

As for His words, ﴿Except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: "Al-'Aziz" is the Dominant, whom nothing can overpower. He, glorified and exalted, possesses dominance and might over everyone. When the hypocrites said, ﴿If we return to Al-Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it﴾, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿But might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 8].

As for His words, ﴿Al-Hamid﴾, it means "the Praised." Allah, glorified and exalted, is praised in every circumstance. It was part of the guidance (hady) of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that when something pleasing came to him he would say: "Praise be to Allah, through whose blessing good deeds are completed," and when something else came to him he would say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."[[Ibn Majah (3803) narrated from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he saw what he loved, would say: "Praise be to Allah through whose blessing good deeds are completed," and when he saw what he disliked, he would say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."]] This is what a person should do. At something disliked, he should say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance." As for what we hear from some people, saying, "Praise be to Allah, who alone is praised for what is disliked," this contradicts what the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) has brought. Rather, say what the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance." To say, "He who alone is praised for what is disliked," is as if you are now declaring that you hate what Allah has decreed for you, and this is not appropriate. Rather, it is obligatory for a person to be content with what Allah has decreed for him, whether it grieves him or pleases him, because who decreed it for you? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He is your Lord and you are His servant; He is your owner and you are His possession. So if Allah is the One who decreed what you dislike, do not despair. It is obligatory for you to be content and patient, and not to be discontented, neither in your heart, nor with your tongue, nor with your limbs. Be patient and endure, for the matter will pass; permanence of a state is impossible. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease."[[Narrated by Ahmad (2803) and al-Tabarani (11243), with this wording, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

So, regarding His words, Exalted and Majestic, ﴿Al-Hamid﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿Al-Hamid﴾? Answer me.

* Students: The Praised.

* The Shaykh: The one praised in every circumstance, whether in ease or hardship, because if He decrees ease, it is a trial and a test. Allah says: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good, as a trial﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 35].

When Sulayman saw the throne of Bilqis placed before him in an instant, what did he say? ﴿This is from the favor of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [An-Naml 40]. So you, my brother, when you are given a blessing, do not take it as merely a blessing so that you become arrogant and exultant. It is indeed a blessing, but know that you are being tested by it: will you fulfill its thanks or not? If hardship befalls you, be patient, for that too is a trial and test from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to see whether you will be patient or not. If you are patient and seek reward from Allah, then Allah says: ﴿Only the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [Az-Zumar 10].

It is also possible that the meaning of His words ﴿Al-Hamid﴾ is another meaning, namely "the One who praises." He, glorified and exalted, praises whoever deserves praise. He commends His servants among the messengers, prophets, and righteous, and commending them is praising them. So He, Exalted, is both the One who praises and the One who is praised. It has been established from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that "Allah is pleased with a servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, and drinks a drink and praises Him for it."[[Narrated by Muslim (2734/89) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "Allah is indeed pleased with the servant who eats a meal..." the hadith.]] This is because, if Allah had not made this meal and drink easy for you, you would not have obtained them. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 63-64]. Answer this question. Allah asks us: ﴿Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ What is the answer?

* The students: Allah.

* The Shaykh: The answer is: Rather, You, O our Lord. ﴿If We willed, We could make it into debris﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 65]. After it comes out and souls become attached to it, Allah makes it debris. He, Mighty and Majestic, did not say, "If We willed, We would not cause it to grow," because its growing, and the soul becoming attached to it, and then it becoming debris, is more painful to the soul than it simply not growing at all. ﴿If We willed, We could make it into debris, and you would be left amazed, saying: "Indeed, we are laden with debt. Rather, we have been deprived."﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 65-67]. Then He came to drinking, saying: ﴿Have you considered the water that you drink? Is it you who brought it down from the clouds, or are We the ones who bring it down?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 68-69]. The answer: Rather, You, O our Lord. ﴿If We willed, We could make it bitter﴾, meaning salty and not sweet, which a person cannot drink. ﴿Then why do you not give thanks?﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 70], meaning: will you not thank Allah for that? Here too, He, Mighty and Majestic, did not say, "If We willed, We would not send it down from the clouds," because its descending and yet not being drinkable is harder to bear than its not descending at all. So reflect, O people of the Noble Qur'an, and you will find in it a great deal of secrets and wisdom.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 85, verse 9:

﴿And they did not resent them except because they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy (8), He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.﴾ [al-Buruj: 8, 9].

﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: Dominion over the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone. None possesses them except Him, the Mighty and Majestic. He owns the heavens and whoever is in them, the earths and whoever is in them, and what is between them and what is in it. Everything is the possession of Allah, and no one shares with Him in His dominion. As for the ownership that is attributed to us, one says, for example: "This house belongs to so-and-so," or "This car belongs to so-and-so." That is a limited ownership, not true ownership. For if a person wished to demolish his house without any reason, would he have the right to do so? Answer me.

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. If you wished to demolish your house without a reason, you could not do this; it is forbidden for you, because the Prophet ﷺ forbade the squandering of wealth.

If you wished to burn your car without a reason, would you have that right? You do not. Even if you did so, people would place you under restraint; the judge would restrict you, preventing you from disposing of your property, although Allah had already restrained you beforehand. So our ownership is limited, and complete ownership belongs to Allah. ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness﴾: He, the Mighty and Majestic, is aware of everything, and among what He is aware of is what these disbelievers do to the believers by burning them with fire, and He will recompense them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 85, verse 10:

But despite that, and despite their committing this hideous act, He said: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning.﴾ [al-Buruj 10]. Some of the early generation (al-salaf) said: Look at the forbearance (hilm) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: they burn His friends, and then He offers them repentance. He says: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell﴾, and if they repent, there is nothing upon them. So reflect, my brother, on the forbearance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: these disbelievers burn His friends, and burning is the most severe form of torture, yet He says: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women﴾.

The scholars said: ﴿fatanu﴾ means "burned," as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Day they will be tried over the Fire. "Taste your trial; this is what you were seeking to hasten."﴾ [adh-Dhariyat 13-14]. These people burned the believing men and the believing women; they would bring a man or a woman and burn them in the fire.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿then they did not repent﴾, i.e., they did not return to Allah, ﴿then they will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning﴾, because they burned the friends of Allah; so their recompense was like their deed, a fitting recompense.

Among the lessons in these verses: Allah, glorified and exalted, may give His enemies power over His friends. So do not be surprised if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, empowers the disbelievers over the believers, so that they kill them, burn them, and violate their honor. Do not be surprised; Allah the Exalted has wisdom in this. The believers who are afflicted have a great reward with Allah, and these aggressive disbelievers, Allah the Exalted gives them respite and leads them step by step to destruction from where they do not know.

The remaining Muslims have a lesson and an admonition in what has befallen their brothers. For example, we now hear what is happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina of great violations: violation of honor, destruction of property, starving of children and the elderly. We hear things that bring tears, and we say: Glory be to Allah! What is this domination that Allah has given over these believers?!

We say: O my brother, do not be surprised. Allah the Exalted has set forth examples for us about those who came before, who burned believers in the fire. So those who have been empowered over our brothers in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in other lands of the Muslims... do not be surprised. This is an elevation of ranks for the afflicted and an expiation of sins, and it is a lesson for those who remain. We must take heed. It is also an enticement for these disbelievers, so that they will be empowered, and then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will seize them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

Among the lessons in these verses: these disbelievers held nothing against the Muslims except one thing, that they believe in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy. This is not a sin; rather, this is the truth, and whoever denies it is the one who should be denounced.

We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to grant victory to the Muslims everywhere, to protect us from the evil of our enemies, and to turn their plotting back against their own necks. Indeed, He is over all things capable.

(...) To proceed: this is the third meeting in the month of Jumada al-Thaniyah of the year fourteen hundred and four, which takes place every Thursday. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to benefit us all by it, to grant us and you beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and to cause us to die in faith.
In our first meetings we chose to speak on the tafsir of Surat an-Naba', because this final part of the Noble Book is recited often, so we chose that people should have knowledge of it, since the benefit of the Qur'an is contemplation (tadabbur) and admonition (ittiʿaz), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A Book We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾ [Sad 29].

We have reached His saying, the Exalted, in Surat al-Buruj: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning﴾ [al-Buruj 10]. "Fatanu" means: they burned them, according to the saying of some people of knowledge, because these criminals dug trenches (akhadid), that is, they cut tunnels (sarادib) in the earth, lit fires in them, and burned the believers in them. So the meaning of ﴿fatanu al-mu'minin﴾ is: they burned the believers. It was also said: "fatanuhum" means: they turned them away from their religion. The correct view is that the verse includes both meanings together, because we should know that the meanings of the Qur'an are broader than our understanding; the meanings of the Qur'an are broader than our understanding, and however much intelligence and perception we attain, we will never encompass it in knowledge; we only know what is made easy for us from it. The rule in the science of tafsir is that if a verse may bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is taken to both. So we say: they tried the believers by turning them away from the way of Allah, and they also tried them by burning.

However, with this, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿then they did not repent﴾, so the noble verse indicates that if they repented, Allah would forgive them, even if they did to His friends what they did; Allah accepts their repentance, because Allah says: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾ [ash-Shura 25].

﴿Then they will have the punishment of Hell﴾, i.e., the punishment of the Fire by which they are tormented; ﴿and they will have the punishment of the Burning﴾, they will be burned in the fire of Hell. We ask Allah for well-being.

The verse alludes to the fact that repentance demolishes what came before it. But, my brothers, we must know that repentance is not a sincere (nasuh) repentance acceptable to Allah unless it includes five conditions:

The first: sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, such that what moves a person to repent is fear of Allah and hope for His reward. A person may repent from sin in order to be praised by people, or to avert people's blame, or for a rank he reaches, or for wealth he obtains. None of these repentances are accepted. Why? Because repentance must be purely for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As for one who intends by his deed the worldly life, Allah says in His Book: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire﴾ [Hud 15-16].

The second of the conditions for repentance to be sincere: regret (nadam) over the sin committed; meaning that a person should not be as though he had not sinned, neither feeling remorse nor sorrow. He must regret; when he remembers the greatness of Allah, he feels regret: how can I disobey my Lord who created me, provided for me, and guided me? So he regrets, just as if a person disobeyed his father, he would regret.

The third: that he desist from the sin (iqla'). Repentance is not valid while persisting in sin, because the one who repents is the one who returns. If a person says, "I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him from consuming usury (riba)," but he still continues to practice usury, is his repentance valid? No, his repentance is not valid.

If he says, "I seek Allah's forgiveness from backbiting (ghibah)," and backbiting is mentioning your brother with what he dislikes, but in every gathering he backbites people, is his repentance valid? No. How can it be valid while he persists in disobedience? He must desist.

If he repents from consuming people's wealth, having stolen from this one and taken the wealth of that one through deception and fraud, is his repentance valid? No, until he returns it, until he returns what he took from people's wealth to the people.

Suppose a person extended his boundary markers into his neighbor's property and seized a part of his land, and said, "I repent." What do we say to him? Return the markers to their original boundaries, or otherwise your repentance will not be accepted, because there must be desisting from the sin he repents of.

The fourth condition: that he firmly resolves not to return to the sin. If he repents while in his heart, were the opportunity to arise, he would return to the sin, his repentance is not accepted. Rather, he must resolve with a firm determination not to return.

The fifth condition: that the repentance occur at a time when repentance is accepted, because there are times when repentance is not accepted. Pay attention to this last condition: there are times when a person's repentance is not accepted, and that is in two states:

The first state: when death approaches him, his repentance is not accepted, due to the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit misdeeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [an-Nisa' 18]. After he has witnessed death and seen the punishment, he says, "I have repented?!" This does not benefit.

A concrete example of this matter: when Pharaoh was overtaken by drowning, what did he say? ﴿He said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed"﴾ [Yunus 90]; meaning, in Allah. He did not say "I believe in Allah," out of self-humiliation, since he had been fighting the Children of Israel for believing in Allah; and now he says: "I believe in what they believed in," as if he made himself a follower of whom? Of the Children of Israel. To this degree humiliation had reached him. Yet it was said to him: ﴿Now?!﴾ Now you repent? Now you believe in what the Children of Israel believed in?! ﴿And you had disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus 91]. So when death approaches, repentance is not accepted.

I ask each one of you: does anyone know when death will come to him?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: No. Therefore, one must hasten to repentance, because you do not know at what time death will come upon you. Do you not know that among people is one who slept on his bed in health and well-being, and then was carried from his bed to the washing bier? We know this has happened. Do you not know that some people sat on their work chair working, then were carried from the work chair to the washing bier? All of this has occurred. So it is necessary that we hasten to repentance, that we hasten to it. We ask Allah to help me and you in that. Hasten to repentance before the doors are closed. Hasten.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿then they did not repent﴾. We have said that repentance is not accepted in two states:

The first state: when death approaches him.

The second state: when the sun rises from its west; when the sun rises from the west and people see it, they believe, but Allah says: ﴿No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith﴾ [al-An'am 158].

So the conditions for the acceptance of repentance are five; we ask Allah to help us and you to realize them.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ [al-Buruj 11].

When He mentioned the punishment of the criminals, He mentioned the reward of the believers. This is the method followed in what is intended for encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib). The Noble Qur'an, which Allah the Exalted described as ﴿mathani﴾ [az-Zumar 23], is one in which opposite meanings are mentioned: the punishment of the people of the Fire and the bliss of the people of Paradise, the attributes of the believers and the attributes of the disbelievers. This is so that a person may proceed toward Allah the Exalted between fear and hope, recognize Allah's blessing upon him in Islam, and recognize Allah's wisdom in the existence of these disbelieving criminals. ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ We will limit ourselves to this portion and postpone discussion of this verse, God willing, until next week.

* * *
(...) with what we always begin with first from the tafsir of the Noble Qur'an. We have reached His saying, may He be exalted, in Surah al-Buruj: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ ﴿Those who believe﴾ are those who believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its evil. This is faith, as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it when Jibril asked him about faith, and he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its evil."[[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and its wording: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and believe in the decree, its good and its evil."]]

As for His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, the meaning is they performed righteous deeds. Righteous deeds are those built upon sincerity to Allah and following the law of Allah. Whoever does a deed in which he associates someone else with Allah, his deed is rejected, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in what he narrates from his Lord, that He, the Exalted, said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners, free from association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his association."[[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

As for following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whoever does a deed that is not according to the law of Allah, it is invalid and rejected, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) with similar wording, and Muslim (1718/18) with its wording, from the hadith of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her).]] Accordingly, the worship of the showoff (murai), who worships Allah but shows off to people, that is, displays worship so that people see him and praise him, does not intend to draw near to people but intends to draw near to Allah, yet wants people to praise him for his drawing near to Allah and his worship of Allah, such a person is a show-off and his deed is also rejected. Likewise, whoever speaks words, Qur'an or remembrance, and raises his voice so that people hear him and praise him for his remembrance of Allah, this is also showing off, and his deed is rejected, because he associated others with Allah in it; he wanted people to praise him for worshipping Allah.

As for whoever worships people, this is a major association (shirk akbar); that is, whoever prays in front of a person out of veneration for him rather than for Allah, and bows and prostrates to the person, this is major association that takes one out of the religion. Likewise, whoever innovates in the religion of Allah what is not part of it, such as if he arranges specific remembrances at a specific time, that is not accepted from him, even if it is the remembrance of Allah; if it is glorification (tasbih), praise (tahmid), magnification (takbir), or declaration of Allah's oneness (tahlil), but he arranged it in a manner for which the Sunnah did not come, that is not accepted by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because he did a deed upon which there is no command of Allah and His Messenger. The main point is that Allah conditioned righteous deeds alongside faith.

From this we know that we should not always focus on creed, saying: we are upon the Islamic creed, upon such and such, and not mention action, because mere creed is not sufficient; there must be action. When you state that we are upon the Islamic creed, you should say: and we do righteous deeds, because Allah always joins faith, which includes creed, with righteous deeds, so that a person is not free of righteous action. As for mere creed, it does not benefit. If a person says: I believe in Allah, but he does not act, where is the faith in Allah?! For this reason, the preponderant view among the scholars is that one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever in a way that takes him out of the religion, and we have explained the evidences for this in a small treatise of ours. Likewise, questions on this subject come up for us in Nur 'ala ad-Darb, and we clarify the evidences in a way that suffices without repeating them here.

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: ﴿for them﴾ means with Allah, ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, and that is after the resurrection; they enter these gardens in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [as-Sajdah 17]. And Allah said in the hadith qudsi: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[[Narrated by Muslim (2825/5) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd as-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him).]] This is because in it is bliss that a person cannot imagine. Allah, the Exalted, mentions in it (i.e., the gardens) palm trees, pomegranates, fruit, the flesh of birds, honey, milk, water, and wine; but do not think that the realities of these things are like the realities of what is in this world at all. For if their realities were like the realities of what is in the world, we would know what has been hidden from us of this. Rather, they are far greater, far greater than you can imagine. Thus the pomegranate, although we know the meaning of pomegranate and know that it has a certain shape, a certain taste, and certain seeds, the pomegranate of the Hereafter is not like this; it is far greater, neither in size, nor in color, nor in taste. Rather, as Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "There is nothing in this world of what is in Paradise except the names alone."[[Narrated by Hannad in az-Zuhd (3) from him, with the wording: "There is nothing in Paradise of what is in this world except the names."]] As for the realities, they are unknown.

As for His saying ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, the scholars said: ﴿beneath them﴾ means beneath its trees and palaces. Otherwise, they are on the surface, above. Furthermore, the hadiths report that these rivers do not need digging, nor need a trench built for them.[[Abu Nu'aym narrated in al-Hilyah (6/205) from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps you think that the rivers of Paradise are a trench in the earth. No, by Allah, they flow over the surface of the earth, their banks are tents of pearl, and their clay is musk, the pure fragrant musk." I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is al-adhfar? He said: "That which has no admixture with it." It was also narrated by Ibn Abi ad-Dunya in Sifat al-Jannah (69) from Anas as a mawquf report.]] Concerning this, Ibn al-Qayyim said in his Nuniyyah:

Its rivers flow without a trench, glory be to Him who holds them back from overflowing.

Rivers, as we commonly know them, need digging or a trench that prevents the water from spreading right and left. But in Paradise they need no trench; they flow wherever a person wishes, that is, he directs them as he wills without digging and without constructing a trench. The rivers here and in many verses are general, but they are detailed in Surah al-Qital, Surah Muhammad: ﴿The parable of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15].
﴿beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph﴾: ﴿That﴾ refers to the gardens and the bliss in them.

﴿The great triumph﴾ means: that by which one is saved from every dreaded thing and attains every sought thing; for triumph is the attainment of what is sought and the removal of what is disliked, and the Garden likewise contains every sought thing, and from it every dreaded thing has been removed. Therefore they will not taste death in it, nor sickness, nor illness, nor sorrow, nor fatigue. We ask Allah to make us and you among its people.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ [Al-Buruj 12-13].

﴿Batsh﴾ means: His seizing (of the wrongdoer) through punishment is severe, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 98]. So the batsh (seizing, i.e. the vengeance and retribution) of Allah is severe and mighty, but it is for those who deserve it. As for those who do not deserve it, the mercy of Allah the Exalted is broader. How often does Allah pardon sins! How often does Allah conceal faults! How often does Allah ward off calamities! And how often do blessings flow! But when He seizes the wrongdoer, He does not let him go, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him escape," and he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ [Hud 102] [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4686), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2583/61), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Based on this, we say: ﴿The seizing of your Lord﴾ means: towards those who deserve seizing. As for one who does not deserve it, Allah the Exalted treats him with mercy, treats him with generosity, and treats him with bounty, and the mercy of Allah the Exalted has preceded His anger.

Verse 13: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ It means that the matter of origination and of return belongs to Him. This is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it﴾ [al-Rum 27]. He is the One who began things, and to Him things return. Things come from Him and go back to Him, in every matter: creation is from Allah and returns to Him, the legislated laws (al-shara'i') are from Allah and return to Him, and all affairs are from Allah and return to Him. For this reason He said ﴿yubdi'u﴾ without mentioning what it is that He originates. Its meaning is: He originates everything and He repeats everything, so the whole matter is in the hand of the Mighty and Majestic. So know your origin, where you come from, and that you began from nothingness; and know your end and goal, and that your goal is toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 85, verse 14:**

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats (13). And He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Loving (14), Owner of the Throne, the Glorious (15).﴾ [Al-Buruj: 13–15] ﴿He is the Most Forgiving﴾ means the Possessor of forgiveness. Forgiveness (maghfirah) is the concealing of a sin and pardoning it. Forgiveness is therefore not merely concealing the sin, but concealing it and not holding the sinner accountable for it, as in the authentic hadith: "Allah will draw near to His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection, and will make him acknowledge his sins until he admits them and confesses. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.'"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4685), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2768/52), from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: While Ibn 'Umar was performing tawaf, a man approached and said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman," or he said, "O Ibn 'Umar, did you hear the Prophet ﷺ speak about private conversation (najwa) with Allah?" He said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The believer will be brought near to his Lord,' and Hisham said: 'the believer will draw near, until He places His screen (kanaf) over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: Do you know such-and-such a sin? He will say: I know. He will say: My Lord, I know. Twice. Then He will say: I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today. Then the record of his good deeds will be unrolled. As for the others, or the disbelievers, they will be called out before the witnesses: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Ah, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 18].']]. Our sins are many: sins of the heart, sins of speech, and sins of action. How numerous they are! Yet Allah, the Exalted, by His praise, conceals them.

It is related that when one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would find it written on the door of his house, as a disgrace and shame, and we seek refuge with Allah from that. But as for us, by Allah's praise, Allah has concealed our sins. Turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness for the sin, and its traces will be completely erased. For this reason He said: ﴿And He is the Most Forgiving﴾, meaning the One who conceals the sins of His servants and overlooks them.

﴿Al-Wadud (the Most Loving)﴾ is derived from wudd, and wudd is pure love. He, Mighty and Majestic, is Wadud.

What is the meaning of (Wadud)? Does it mean that He is loved, or that He loves?

The answer is that it includes both meanings. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion - Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54]. So He, Mighty and Majestic, is Wadd (One who loves): He loves deeds, He loves persons, and He loves places. He is also Mahbub (One who is loved), loved by His allies: ﴿Say, if you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 31]. The more a person follows the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the more beloved he is to Allah. So He, Mighty and Majestic, is Wadd, and He is also Wadud (One who is loved), meaning that He loves and is loved. The Exalted loves deeds, loves the doers, and loves persons. That is, the love of Allah may be attached to a specific person, as in the words of the Messenger, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on the day of Khaybar: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." The people spent the night, then in the morning all of them went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hoping to be given it. He said: "Where is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib?" They said: "He has an eye complaint." So he called for him, and he came. He spat in his eyes, and he was healed as if he had never had any pain. Then he gave him the banner and said: "Proceed calmly until you reach their courtyard, then invite them to Islam."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3009), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2406/36), from Sahl, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Khaybar: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man through whose hands Allah will grant victory, one who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." The people spent that night wondering which of them would be given it. In the morning they all came hoping for it. He said: "Where is 'Ali?" It was said: "He has an eye complaint." He spat in his eyes and prayed for him, and he was healed as if he had never had any pain. He gave him the banner. 'Ali said: "Shall I fight them until they become like us?" He said: "Proceed calmly until you reach their courtyard, then invite them to Islam, and inform them of what is incumbent upon them. By Allah, if Allah guides one man through you, it is better for you than red camels."]]. The evidence is his words: "He loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him." Here he affirmed that Allah loves this specific man, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

When the Prophet ﷺ sent a man in command of a sariyyah (a military expedition led by a single commander) he would lead them in prayer, and end his recitation with (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad). When they returned to the Prophet ﷺ, they told him about this, because his practice was not well known, namely that a person, whenever he recites in prayer, makes his final recitation (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad). He said: "Ask him why he does that." They asked him, and he said: "It is the attribute of Allah, and I love to recite it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Tell him that Allah loves him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7375) and Muslim (813/263), from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man in command of a sariyyah. He used to recite for his companions in their prayers and conclude with (Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad). When they returned, this was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Ask him why he does that." They asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Tell him that Allah loves him."]]. Here you see that the love is attached to a specific person: the love of Allah.

The love of Allah may also be attached to certain people by their qualities, as in: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾ [At-Tawbah: 4], ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 195], and ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a compact structure﴾ [As-Saff: 4]. Here there is no specific person, but there is a person described by a quality.

Likewise, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, loves places. The most beloved of lands to Allah are its mosques.[[Narrated by Muslim (671/288) from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most beloved of lands to Allah are its mosques, and the most hated of lands to Allah are its markets."]] The Prophet, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, also informed us that Makkah is the most beloved of places to Allah.[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (4240) from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while he was in the market of al-Hazwarah in Makkah: "By Allah, you are the best of the lands of Allah and the most beloved of lands to Allah. Had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left."]] This love is attached to places. Allah, the Exalted, loves and is loved, and for this reason He said: ﴿And He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Loving﴾.

Then He explained His greatness and the completeness of His dominion in His saying: ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious. (15) Doer of whatever He intends.﴾ [Al-Buruj 15-16]. "Owner of the Throne" means the possessor of the Throne, and the Throne is that upon which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is established. It is the greatest, largest and most spacious of creation. It has been reported in a narration (athar) that the seven heavens and the seven earths, in comparison to the Kursi (Footstool), are like a ring cast into a desert plain, a small ring of armor cast into a desert plain, which is nothing in comparison to it, and that the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert plain over that ring[[Ibn Hibban (361) narrated from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The seven heavens with the Kursi are nothing but like a ring thrown down in a desert plain, and the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert plain over the ring..." The hadith.]]. So no one can estimate the vastness of the Kursi. If we observe among the visible creatures now the tremendous disparity in their sizes, then consider: a man showed me a picture of the sun, a photograph, and a picture of the earth, and I found that the earth, in relation to this sun, is like a point, not large, in a vast and great expanse, and that it is not attributed to the sun at all, it is nothing. If this is the case with visible things that are perceived by the telescope and other instruments, then what about things hidden from us! For what is hidden from us is greater than what we see. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ [Al-Isra 85]. The conclusion is that the Throne is this which is the ceiling of all creatures, a great Throne, upon which the Most Merciful is established, the Exalted; as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne.﴾ [Ta-Ha 5].

As for His saying: ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾, there are two readings for it: ﴿الْمَجِيدِ﴾ (al-Majidi) and ﴿الْمَجِيدُ﴾ (al-Majidu). On the first reading it is an attribute of the Throne, and on the second it is an attribute of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and both are correct. The Throne is glorious, and likewise the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is glorious; and we say in the tashahhud: "Indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 85, verse 16:

﴿Doer of whatever He wills﴾. Whatever He wills, He does, glorified and exalted is He, because His authority is complete; no one can prevent Him, none can reverse His judgment, and none can repel His decree. ﴿And when Allah intends harm for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have not besides Him any protector﴾ [al-Ra'd 11]. So whatever He wills, He does. But the kings of this world, however great their dominion, do not do everything they wish; how often do they want something and then some obstacle arises to prevent it. As for the Lord, He is the possessor of the greatest authority, whose will is not turned back by anything: ﴿Doer of whatever He wills﴾. This is evidence that everything that occurs in the universe occurs by the will of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, because it is Allah who created it, so it exists by His will. However, know that Allah does not will anything except for a wisdom, so every act of Allah is for a great wisdom, some of which we know and some of which we do not know.

We pause at this noble verse, and we ask Allah, exalted is He, to make us and you among those who recite His Book with its due recitation, to grant us understanding of it, and to help us act upon it. Indeed, He is Most Generous, Most Noble.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 85, verse 19:

(...) Our meeting today includes the explanation of the remainder of "al-Buruj" (the Constellations), ﴿And by the sky containing the mansions of the stars﴾, and of the questions that arise, which we answer with the success granted by Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

We have reached the words of Allah, blessed and exalted, in Surah al-Buruj: ﴿But those who disbelieve are in denial, and Allah encompasses them from behind them﴾ [al-Buruj 19-20]. ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ includes everyone who disbelieves in Allah and His Messenger, whether he be of the polytheists, the Jews, the Christians, or others. This is because the Jews and the Christians, now and after the mission of the Messenger ﷺ, are not upon a religion, and their religions do not benefit them, for he (i.e., the Prophet ﷺ) is the Seal of the Prophets. Whoever does not believe in him is not upon anything of his religion. Moreover, it has already been mentioned that whoever does not believe in one of the messengers is a disbeliever in all the messengers. For example, whoever does not believe that Noah is a messenger, even if he believes in other prophets, is a denier of all the prophets. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 105]. Allah clarified that these people denied all the messengers, although they had denied only one messenger, since there was no messenger before Noah. Likewise, whoever denies Muhammad ﷺ is a denier of the other messengers. So if the Jews claim that they are upon a religion and that they follow the Torah brought by Moses, we say to them: You are disbelievers in Moses, disbelievers in the Torah. And if the Christians, who call themselves Christians today, claim that they believe in Jesus, we say to them: You lie; you are disbelievers in Jesus, because you disbelieve in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

It is strange that these Jews and Christians disbelieve in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, although they ﴿find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and makes unlawful for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them﴾ [al-A'raf 157], and ﴿they recognize him as they recognize their own sons﴾ [al-Baqarah 146]. But stubbornness, arrogance and envy prevented them from believing in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾ [al-Baqarah 109]. The conclusion is that the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿But those who disbelieve﴾ include everyone who disbelieves in Muhammad, even among the Jews and the Christians. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 85, verses 21–22:

﴿Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an, (21) in a preserved tablet.﴾ [al-Buruj: 21, 22].

Describing the Qur'an as glorious does not mean that glory is an attribute of the Qur'an alone; rather, it is an attribute of the Qur'an and of the one who bears this Qur'an, carries it, and fulfils his duty toward it by reciting it as it truly should be recited. Such a person will have glory, honour and elevation.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾ mean the preserved tablet with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which is the Mother of the Book, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Allah effaces what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 39].

If someone asks us: "Of what material is this tablet?" What do we say?

* A student: We say: Allah knows best.

* The Shaykh: We say: Allah knows best. That is, if he asks: Is it of wood? Of iron? Of glass? Of gold? Of silver? We do not know. It is a tablet in which Allah wrote the decrees of everything, and among what He wrote in it is that this Qur'an would be sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ. So it is ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾.

The scholars said: ﴿preserved﴾ means no one can reach it; it is preserved from alteration and change. Alteration and change occur only in the other books, because writing from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is of several kinds, and I hope you will pay attention to this:

The first kind: writing in the Preserved Tablet. This writing is not changed or altered, and for this reason Allah named it a preserved tablet; what is in it cannot be changed or altered, because it is the final determination.

The second: writing concerning the children of Adam while they are in their mothers' wombs. When a human being in the womb has completed four months, Allah sends to him an angel entrusted with the wombs, and he breathes the spirit into him by Allah's permission, for the body is merely a piece of flesh; when the spirit is breathed into it, it becomes a human being. He is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term of life, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or happy.[[Al-Bukhari (3208) and Muslim (2643/1) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the truthful and the believed, related to us: "Indeed, each of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days, then becomes a clot of blood for a like period, then becomes a lump of flesh for a like period, then Allah sends an angel who is commanded with four words and it is said to him: Write his deeds, his provision, his term, and whether he is wretched or happy..." The hadith.]]

There is another writing that occurs yearly, which is the writing that takes place on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr). Allah, Glorified and Exalted, determines in this night what will happen in that year. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Therein is decreed every wise matter﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 4], so in this night is written what will occur in that year.

There is a fourth writing, which is the writing of the scrolls in the hands of the angels. This writing occurs after the deed, whereas the three previous writings are all before the deed. This last writing is written on the person what he does of speech by his tongue, action by his limbs, or belief by his heart. The angels entrusted with guarding the children of Adam, that is, guarding their deeds, write; Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Nay! But you deny the Recompense. (9) And indeed, over you are guardians, (10) noble recorders, (11) who know whatever you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 9–12].

However, this last writing differs from the three previous writings, because it is writing after the deed, so that what the person did is recorded upon him. On the Day of Resurrection he will be given this book, as Allah says: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread open. (13) Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 13, 14]. That is, you are given the book and it is said: You, read and take account of yourself. Some of the early scholars said: "Whoever made you a reckoner over yourself has been fair to you." This is true. What fairness could be more eloquent than to say to a person: Here, this is what you did; take account of yourself? Is this not fairness? The greatest fairness is this. On the Day of Resurrection you will be given this book open before you, not closed; you will read it, and it will become clear to you that on such a day, in such a place, you did such and such. It is precise and does not change. And if you deny it here, who will bear witness against you? ﴿On the Day when their tongues will testify against them﴾: the tongue says, "I spoke such-and-such"; ﴿their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [an-Nur: 24]. The hand says, "I struck"; the foot says, "I walked." Indeed, the skins also testify to what they touched: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned"﴾ [Fussilat: 21].

The main point now is that the Preserved Tablet is this tablet in which Allah wrote the decrees of everything. It is preserved from change and preserved from anyone reaching it, and Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows what is written in it. We have said that it is preserved because it does not change, whereas what is in the hands of the angels changes. We have said that the writings are four: the Preserved Tablet; second, the writing of embryos; third, the yearly writing on the Night of Decree; and fourth, the writing of deeds after they occur, which is in the hands of the angels: one angel on the right and one on the left, recording everything the person says.

We are now recording in a recorder on a tape, and not a single word of our speech is lost; even the breath is captured by this tape. They, the angels too, write everything: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18]. As for ﴿any word﴾, the scholars of rhetoric say that an indefinite noun in the context of negation denotes generality: whatever word you say, there is with you an observer, ready and present, who is never absent from you.

It is mentioned that Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, was ill, and he was moaning during his illness because of the severity of the sickness. One of his companions entered upon him and said: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, Tawus, who is a well-known man among the Tabi'un, says that the angels write down for a person even the moaning of illness, even his moaning during his sickness." So he, may Allah have mercy on him, refrained from moaning. The matter is not a light one. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to take charge of us and of you with His pardon and forgiveness.

Here the discussion of this great surah ends, the surah which Allah began with an oath by the heaven of the mansions of the stars and concluded with His words: ﴿Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an, (21) in a preserved tablet﴾ [al-Buruj: 21, 22]. Whoever holds fast to this mighty Qur'an, for him is glory, honour, dignity and elevation. For this reason we advise our Islamic Ummah, beginning with the individuals of its peoples, to hold fast to the mighty Qur'an, and we direct the call with greater and greater emphasis to the rulers of its affairs to hold fast to the mighty Qur'an, and not to be deceived by the glittering finery that comes from the disbelieving nations which produce laws contrary to the Shari'ah, contrary to justice, contrary to the reform of creation, and put them into implementation, then cast the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger behind their backs. By Allah, this is the cause of backwardness. I do not think anyone now imagines that a nation of such vast number would be so backward, as though it were a small emirate in a village compared with the disbelieving states. But the cause of that is, without doubt, known: we have abandoned what gives us our might and dignity, which is holding fast to this mighty Qur'an, and we have gone panting after perishing, corrupt systems that oppose justice and are built on oppression and tyranny.

So we appeal to the rulers of our affairs, and by "rulers of our affairs" I mean the rulers of all Muslims, because we are one Ummah even if lands divide us and tongues differ among us. We appeal to them to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to return in genuine return to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, so that security and stability may be established for them, that might, glory and elevation may be attained, that their peoples may obey them, and that there be no resentment in the hearts of their peoples toward them. This is because when a person sets right what is between him and his Lord, Allah sets right what is between him and the people. If the rulers want their peoples to submit to them and to obey Allah concerning them, then let them first obey Allah, so that their nations may obey them. Otherwise, it is not reasonable that they disobey the Supreme King, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and then want their peoples to obey them. That is far-fetched. Indeed, the more the heart drifts from Allah, the more people drift from its companion—we ask Allah for well-being—and the closer one draws to Allah, the closer people draw to him. We ask Allah to restore to this Islamic Ummah its glory and dignity, to humble the enemies of the Muslims everywhere, and we ask Allah, the Exalted, to aid our Muslim brothers in Bosnia and Herzegovina and to help them against what has befallen them from these Christians who do not want any Muslim standing anywhere, and we ask Allah to humble the Christians and the Jews, to subdue them, to frustrate them and to return them on their heels defeated, and likewise every enemy of the Muslims. Indeed, He is powerful over all things.
